title: UNDERNEATH
author: Ensemble
phase: convening (after cycle 007): a pilot for the Studio's proposed question
question: What does the world record of the catastrophes that almost happened, and who decides that a near miss counts?
proposed_question: Who stood beneath the catastrophes that almost happened, and what does the world record of the people a near miss was held over?
medium: A globe with sound that turns to each of the thirteen asteroid impacts predicted before they struck (2008-2026), zooms to a 50 km circle around the point, shades the night at the minute of impact, and, while a clock runs the hours between first sighting and strike, fills the circle with one dot per thousand estimated residents; a drone for the held hours, a tick per hour, a thump at the strike. A bar figure of the held hours by people beneath; the Field's warning clock with the thirteen written above it.
embodies: THE MINUTE WAS KNOWN; THE PEOPLE WERE NOT COUNTED. 13 times the record named the minute and the point of a strike, 1.8 to 20.8 hours ahead. 6 came down within 50 km of people, about 2,864,000 of them by a 2020 grid, all 6 in the dark. No record read counts who beneath was told.
form: An orthographic globe, a clock, dots, sound; two figures.
form_argument: The missing datum is a count of people over a span of hours. Only a work that runs those hours, compressed, and lets the people arrive while the record holds its minute makes the gap between the two felt; the globe's night shows when they were.
the_rule_the_work_kept: Times, points and surveys only from the cited list, checked against JPL's fireball record where it has a located entry; residents only as a stated estimate (WorldPop 2020, 50 km disc, the work's own convention), never a danger zone; dot positions declared not data; no claim that no one was told, only that no record read counts it; the Field's clock taken unchanged at a pinned commit.

siblings.field: Seen coming (study 11, 2026-10-13): built on. Its warning clock for 1,015 close passages 2015-2025 is the work's second figure, unchanged; the thirteen warnings that came true are written above it by the same whole-day rule (9 on day 0, 4 on day 1). Its proposal asks who keeps the warnings; this asks who they were kept over.
siblings.atelier: Nobody's Minute (convening pilot, 2026-10-13): the credit for a prevented catastrophe goes to whoever tells it afterwards. Here nothing needed preventing; the work asks for whom the record was kept while it was being kept.

atlas_neighbours.title: Of All the People in All the World: Stats with Rice
atlas_neighbours.daylight: There a grain stands for each person in a statistic someone already took. Here the people were never counted: the dots are this work's estimate standing in for a count the record of a predicted impact does not hold, and they exist only for the hours the warning was held.

atlas_neighbours.title: Missing Datasets (list/essay)
atlas_neighbours.daylight: There uncollected datasets are listed. Here one missing count is estimated and made to arrive in time beside the record that could have taken it.
